title: What If a Diver Rose to the Surface Too Fast?

scenes.text: What if a diver shot to the surface? The gas in their body turns on them.
Underwater, pressure pushes extra nitrogen from every breath into your blood and tissues.
Rise slowly and you breathe it out. The US Navy and NOAA use about 30 feet a minute.
Rise too fast and the dissolved gas forms bubbles, a bit like fizz in a shaken soda.
Bubbles can block blood flow. The first sign is usually pain near a joint, which is why it's called the bends.
The cure is a pressure chamber that squeezes you back down, then brings you up slowly. The hard part of a dive is the way back up.
